cliQuirks.--lang de --help: exit 0 with English help before language validation
cliQuirks.--lang de --version: exit 0 with English output before language validation

differences: Bash ships complete catalogs for all six languages; Go has complete catalogs only for zh and en.
Bash falls back to English per missing message (_xray_i18n_setup); Go falls back for the whole language and prints one notice.
Bash and Go read etc/idleleo/language.conf; Go also offers explicit language show/set commands and --lang overrides the stored default.
Bash renders a localized 45-column adaptive menu box; Go renders an English single-line prompt with no width adaptation (not aligned).
Bash suppresses ANSI without a TTY or with NO_COLOR; Go never emits ANSI, which is stricter rather than a parity gap.
narrowScreenParity: not aligned: Go help is a single unwrapped block wider than 80 columns
ttyMenuParity: not aligned: Go menu prompt stays English and has no 45-column layout
